# Data Leakage

Data leakage occurs when training or evaluation uses information unavailable at the real prediction time, or when evaluation data influences model selection improperly.

## Examples
- Scaling all rows before splitting the dataset.

Threshold selection depends on the cost of false positives and false negatives. See [[Logistic Regression]] and [[Churn Prediction Experiment]].

Training commonly minimizes binary cross-entropy. A decision threshold converts probabilities into class predictions; 0.5 is a convention, not a requirement.

In [[Churn Prediction Experiment]], a lower threshold may find more customers who will leave, while increasing false positives. Evaluate that tradeoff using [[Classification Metrics]].

Scaling and regularization can improve training stability. Compare with [[Decision Trees]].

- Select the threshold on validation data.
- Reserve the final test partition until model selection is complete.

- What is the operational cost of a false-positive outreach?
- Does performance differ by plan type?

A random forest combines many decision trees trained with randomized sampling. Typical implementations bootstrap training examples and consider a subset of features at each split.

Averaging predictions reduces variance compared with an individual deep tree. Forests can model nonlinear interactions with limited preprocessing.

| Precision | TP / (TP + FP) | How many positive predictions were correct? |
| Recall | TP / (TP + FN) | How many actual positives were found? |
| F1 | 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall) | What is their harmonic mean? |
| Accuracy | correct predictions / all predictions | What fraction of all predictions was correct? |

Handle zero denominators explicitly. Accuracy can hide poor minority-class performance when classes are imbalanced.

Use training data to fit model parameters, validation data to choose hyperparameters, and test data for a final held-out estimate.

A 70/15/15 split is an illustrative choice, not a universal rule. Small datasets may benefit from cross-validation.

# Overfitting and Regularization

Overfitting occurs when a model captures training-specific noise and performs worse on unseen data. A large gap between training and validation performance is one warning sign.

## Techniques
- L2 regularization penalizes squared coefficient magnitudes.

# Database Indexes

A database index stores an auxiliary structure to accelerate selected lookups. A B-tree index often supports equality and range queries.

Indexes consume storage and add maintenance work during inserts, updates, and deletes. Whether a query uses an index depends on the database, query, statistics, and data distribution.
